薩克布特是文藝復興與巴洛克時期長號的早期形式，由滑管號演變而來，以雙管滑管改變音: The sackbut is the early form of the trombone used in the Renaissance and Baroque, developed from the slide trumpet and changing pitch with a double slide. The earliest record of a slide instrument may be in Burgundy in the 1420s; the word trombone appears about twenty years earlier than sackbut, and the German term is older still. Sackbut was originally a French word; it stayed in use in England until it fell away in the eighteenth century, and when the instrument was revived at the end of that century trombone became the usual name. The form changed little between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries, with a slightly wider bell in the Classical period; after the mid-eighteenth century the bell grew larger, the crook was dropped and the stay became tubular, giving a stronger tone suited to nineteenth-century marching bands. The earliest evidence of a double slide is in Roman frescoes of 1488–1493.
薩克布特長號主要採用黃銅製造管身與滑管，喇叭口同樣為黃銅材質。U形雙管滑管設計中: The sackbut's tube and slide are mainly made of brass, and the bell is brass as well. In the U-shaped double slide, two parallel sliding tubes keep the intonation stable. The mouthpiece is usually of copper or silver. Wooden parts may appear in the handle or the stays. The whole shows the fine metalworking of the Renaissance, with the thickness of the wall and the alloy carefully chosen to produce its warm, soft timbre.

薩克布特長號音色溫潤而柔和，帶有典雅的古典韻味。其音質不如現代長號明亮銳利，反而: The sackbut's timbre is warm and soft, with an elegant, old-fashioned charm. It is not as bright and sharp as the modern trombone; instead it is warm and slightly hoarse, on the dark side and full of a sense of history. The middle register is the most expressive, the low register full and powerful, the high register more restrained. Because the bore is narrow and the bell only moderately flared, the resonance is relatively contained, and the sound does not project the way a modern trombone does. Compared with brass of its own period, the sackbut is closer to the mildness of the old double reeds; compared with trombones of later centuries it has less brilliance and penetration. This particular sound makes it especially suited to Renaissance polyphony, where it produces an elegant, inward ensemble.
薩克布特長號（Sackbut）是長號在文藝復興與巴洛克時期的早期形式，屬氣鳴樂器: The sackbut is the early form of the trombone in the Renaissance and Baroque, an aerophone, Hornbostel-Sachs classification 423.22, sounding by the vibration of the lips. It has a U-shaped slide with two parallel tubes, and the player moves the slide to change the length of the tube and so the pitch; the bore is narrow and the bell less flared. It was used in alta capella bands and appears with the organ and others in Baroque polyphonic works.
